LLM_description:
Situation:
Multiple forward brigades are operating along contested corridors with dispersed positions requiring daily resupply. Rear-area depots (e.g., Supply Depot Bravo, Depot Charlie, Depot Delta) hold limited stocks and must push sustainment forward to maneuver units at Forward Operating Base Alpha, Fire Base Ridge, Combat Outpost Hammer, and other positions. Movement corridors include valley routes and urban chokepoints susceptible to ambush, IEDs, and intermittent indirect fire. Movement windows are constrained by weather, route clearance schedules, and air tasking cycles. Security packages (escort platoons, EOD teams, route clearance patrols, and ISR overwatch) must be coordinated for each activated route.

Mission:
Deliver required supplies from designated depots to all supported units over the planning horizon while minimizing total operational cost, including transport costs, shortage penalties for unmet demand, per-vehicle deployment costs, and fixed route security risk costs.

Execution/Concept:
- Demand fulfillment: Each unit’s daily requirement will be satisfied through planned shipments; controlled shortfalls are permitted where necessary and will be recorded as slack and penalized accordingly.
- Depot constraints: Outbound flows are limited by depot stock availability per day; no depot will exceed its capacity.
- Vehicles and capacity: Shipments must fit within vehicle capacity constraints, accounting for supply volume per unit of measure. Per-vehicle deployment costs apply. Vehicles may only operate on routes that have been activated.
- Route activation and risk: Activating a route on any day, defined as sending any vehicles along that depot-to-unit corridor, incurs a fixed Risk Cost representing the security overhead (escort, clearance, overwatch) for that route, regardless of the number of vehicles dispatched. If a route is not activated, no fixed risk cost is incurred.
- Fleet limits: Total vehicles committed across all routes on any day cannot exceed fleet availability. Convoy size and sequencing will be synchronized with maneuver and route clearance timelines.
- Optimization approach: Select depot-to-unit flows, route activations, and vehicle allocations that minimize the sum of transport costs, shortage penalties, vehicle deployment costs, and fixed route security risk costs, while respecting depot capacities, vehicle load constraints, route activation rules, and fleet limits.
- Priorities: Emphasize resupply to units in contact and critical fires elements, maintaining combat effectiveness while balancing risk exposure and cost.
